reachable: Yes, and in the only way a batcher can be. The impl is loaded solely at evolve/harness.py:78 (`G.load_batcher(genome)(fit_stripped, bs, seed)`) and its output is used only as sequence indices at line 80-83. It changes which sequences appear in each training batch, so it shapes every gradient the net receives, including at the command positions the objective is computed on. It has no path into the scoring instrument: cups_probe / cups_ca build their own tokens from the embedding cache and never call the batcher. The mechanism is therefore not gated on anything about the scored position — it cannot be switched off at the read the way an observation-gated mechanism would be. It also survives the harness's strip seam: `_strip_target_only` removes only exit_cls/z_delta, and the keys the batcher reads ("cmds", "image") are present in every encoded sequence dict (realenv/seq_worldmodel.py:83). The one caveat is leverage, not reachability: the batcher chooses sequences, not steps, and each training sequence carries exactly one cups window among ~30 steps, so its influence on the per-step gradient mix is bounded — a bound the hypothesis states honestly (L82-84).
solves_outside_model: No — this is legitimate sample selection. The impl parses command strings (`_parse_event` / `_read_hops`) to compute a per-sequence hop-depth label, and that label is used only to pick WHICH SEQUENCES go into a training batch. Nothing derived from the parse is written into a token, an embedding, a target, or a loss weight; `next_batch` returns a plain list of integers, and the harness passes those indices to `stream.collate`, which builds tokens from the cached embeddings alone. The resolved routing never reaches the model as input, in training or at scoring. Contrast with the retracted stream candidate: there the resolved identity was stamped into the read command token so the scored input WAS the answer. Here the resolved chain never leaves the batcher's closure. Verified `fit` is not mutated (JSON snapshot identical after 300 batches) and the global torch RNG is untouched (torch.randn after 200 batches bit-identical to a control), so the parse cannot leak through a side channel either.
summary: The code implements the described mechanism faithfully, and every measured number in the hypothesis reproduces — which is notable given the author had no torch. Verified by execution: (1) the symbolic tracker's physics matches the prose clause for clause (`mv` pops the source and adds one hop; `cp` and `cat A > B` copy one hop further leaving the source; `cat A >> B` takes max(hops(B), hops(A)+1); a bare read reports the standing hop count) and no path normalization is present, as claimed. (2) The 24/24 ground-truth check reproduces exactly on evolve/jail_data/train_sample.jsonl, and the tracker is in fact stronger than claimed — it matches meta['cups']['depth'] on 2560/2560 sequences of the real training split, zero mismatches. (3) The frontier `1 + (d_top-1)*ramp` and the asymmetric kernel `exp(-(d-f)/tau_up)` above / `exp(-(f-d)*lam_down)` below are coded exactly as written, sharp above and mild below with tau_up=0.5, lam_down=0.35. (4) `_quota` is correct largest-remainder allocation and cannot overshoot bs; every one of 4000 batches met or exceeded its analytic per-depth quota (0 shortfalls), so "every single batch carries the scheduled depth spectrum" holds. (5) The claimed composition numbers reproduce on the author's own setup (24 jail trajectories replicated to 1920): uniform 50.0% at depth>=3 and 4.17% at the deepest stratum (claimed 50% and 4%); post-ramp 76.5% / 26.0% / 23.5% at depth>=3 / deepest / depths 1-2 (claimed ~78% / 25% / ~20%). (6) Timings reproduce: setup 0.028 s for 1920 sequences (claimed 0.03 s), 0.199 s for 4000 steps at bs=64 (claimed 0.19 s); 0.036 s / 0.204 s on the real 2560-sequence split. (7) All contract claims hold: deterministic given the seed, seed-sensitive, private generator, fit unmutated, exact length and in-bounds across 4000 steps, and all seven named degenerate inputs (bs=1, bs>n, n=1, single image, empty command lists, unparseable commands, curr_frac=0) return valid batches. (8) The inherited image-blocking claim holds on the real split — all 48 (image, depth) blocks are populated, and with curr_frac=1.0 every post-ramp batch draws from exactly one image. The two things that do not match are downstream of the same root cause: the guards that the hypothesis says bound thin-stratum resampling (the room cap and min_stratum) are computed over the GLOBAL stratum while the draw happens inside a single image's block, so the deepest quotas are filled by resampling ~4-6 distinct sequences 11-16 times per batch, and 57.8% of scheduled draws concentrate on 90 sequences (3.5% of the split). And because the frontier ends at d_top=6 while the scored slice is depths 3-4, the post-ramp batch actually carries fewer depth-3/4 windows (20.1) than plain uniform sampling (24.1) — the hypothesis's wording ("depth 3 and deeper") is defensible against cups_ca.DEPTH_MIN=3, but the mechanism's leverage on the scored depths points the opposite way from how the enrichment claim reads. Both are named as risks in the hypothesis's own failure section, which is why this is a divergence in effect rather than in honesty. What I could not check: the effect on comp_ca itself (needs a GPU training run, and the eval's noise floor is 0.0227); behavior under a blended training root (no blend.json is present locally, so I measured the single cups root the adapter defaults to); and whether the heavy within-block repetition of ~90 deep sequences hurts the image-held-out transfer the eval measures.

divergences.claim: "A count is capped at its stratum's size and the freed slots go to the uniform part, so a thin stratum is never resampled to fill a large quota." (hypothesis.txt L38-39), plus "d_top (the deepest stratum holding at least min_stratum sequences)" as the guard against thin deep strata (L26-27).
divergences.what_the_code_does: Both guards are computed GLOBALLY (`room = [len(strata[d])...]`, `big = [d for d in depths if len(strata[d]) >= min_stratum]`) while the actual draw in `_draw` is restricted to the ONE sampled image's `block_pool[(img, d)]` and uses `torch.multinomial(..., replacement=True)`. On the real train split the global cap never binds, so the per-image block is resampled to fill a quota several times its size — exactly the thing the sentence says cannot happen.
divergences.evidence: Measured on data/dockerfs3-cupsF-treat-nocwd/train.jsonl (2560 seqs, 8 images, genome params). End-of-ramp quota over depths 1..6 = [3,4,6,8,11,16] out of n_curr=48. Global room = [737,768,547,418,52,38] — the cap is never reached. Per-image block sizes at depth 6 = [4,2,5,11,4,3,6,3] and at depth 5 = [1,10,4,6,4,6,12,9]. So 16 slots are drawn with replacement from a block of median ~4 sequences, and 11 more from a block of median ~6. With curr_frac=1.0 for isolation, 57.8% of all scheduled draws post-ramp land on the 90 sequences (3.5% of the split) labeled depth 5 or 6; a single sequence is drawn 4530 times across 2600 post-ramp batches. min_stratum=8 admits depth 6 as d_top on the global count of 38 while every per-image block is below 8.

divergences.claim: The framing that the design guarantees deep-window gradient for the scored quantity: "comp_ca is a paired difference on windows of hop depth 3 and deeper" (L46) and "a roughly six-fold enrichment of the deepest stratum with the shallow scaffold retained" (L62).
divergences.what_the_code_does: The frontier walks to d_top = 6 and the kernel puts the largest share on the deepest stratum, so post-ramp the batch is enriched at depths 5-6 — which do not appear in the scored slice — at the expense of depths 3-4, which is where the score is actually taken. Relative to the plain uniform baseline the candidate must beat, per-batch exposure to depth-3/4 windows goes DOWN.
divergences.evidence: Exactly one cups window per training sequence (2560 windows / 2560 seqs), and the tracker's label equals that window's depth for depths 3-6, so per-batch depth-3/4 windows = per-batch sequences labeled 3 or 4. Simulated 4000 steps at bs=64 on the real split: post-ramp batch composition is {1:0.118, 2:0.137, 3:0.147, 4:0.167, 5:0.177, 6:0.254}, i.e. 20.1 depth-3/4 windows per batch, versus uniform sampling's 0.377 -> 24.1 per batch. 43% of post-ramp batch slots sit at depths 5-6. The val slice (style=core, N in 3-5, depth>=3) holds 270 windows of which only 11 are depth>=5, and the scored slice is depths 3 and 4. Note the hypothesis's wording is not literally false — cups_ca.DEPTH_MIN=3 with no upper cap — so this is a design-vs-realized-slice mismatch rather than a misstatement, but a reader of the hypothesis would expect the mechanism to raise exposure to the scored depths and it lowers it.

divergences.claim: "Under i.i.d. block sampling a sizeable share of batches carry almost no deep window at all" (L57-58).
divergences.what_the_code_does: N/A — a characterization of the baseline, not of this code.
divergences.evidence: Under uniform sampling on the real split, 41.2% of sequences are depth>=3, i.e. ~26 deep windows in a 64-batch; no batch carries "almost no deep window". Only the depth-5/6 tail is rare (1.5%, ~1 per batch). The quantitative claims stated immediately after this sentence are correct; the sentence itself overstates.
